sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: Passiflora edulis is a perennial vine native to South America, cultivated for its fruits and sometimes escaped in woodland edges and waste ground. Its climbing stems can reach about 15 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The leaves are deeply three-lobed and about 5–11 cm long. The white flowers, 4–7 cm across, are surrounded by a purple corona. The leathery berry is 4–5 cm across and may be yellow, yellow-green or purple depending on the cultivated form.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The pulp of the ripe fruit is eaten. This species is related to P. incarnata and P. tarminiana, but their fruits and uses are not interchangeable.
